newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan arrests two suspected of spying for China.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan arrests two suspected of spying for China.

text.p: Taiwan prosecutors have arrested two men suspected of spying for arch rival China, and the ruling Nationalist Party on Friday said one of the two had been working for the party in Macao.
"We have sufficient evidence to back our arrest action against the two," Lu Jen-fa, chief prosecutor of the Taipei district court, said on state television.
He said the two men, whom he declined to identify, were detained at a Taipei hotel in February on suspicion of leaking defence secrets to the Chinese communists.
Chang Ching-heng, deputy director and spokesman for the Nationalist Party's overseas affairs department, told Reuters one of the men was a volunteer for the party in the Portuguese enclave of Macao.
"He is...still very active in Macao," Chang said, adding that he did not know how he had gained access to national defence information.
"Even being a deputy director of the party's overseas affairs department, I have no access to national defence secrets," Chang said.
State media said the two were asked to come to Taiwan to meet Wang Neng-chang, director of the overseas affairs department, and were arrested during the meeting.
The United Evening News said the two had been assigned to help the Nationalist government gather information on China in Macao.
In 1995 and 1996, they allegedly leaked information including details on defence strategy and deployment of armed forces to communist Chinese agents in Macao.
China's Nationalists fled to Taiwan at the end of the civil war in 1949 and the two sides have remained rivals ever since.
If convicted, the two men could face jail terms of up to 10 years, court officials said.
